The kernel's validity hinges on legal and data constraints. Legal risk (L) is modeled as a binary condition with approval (A) acting as a gate. Data integrity (D) is enforced via consent (C) and deletion control (T). These primitives form a layered constraint system that ensures safe simulation. Failure modes include unauthorized real-money flow, data leakage, and invalid reward calculation when R exceeds total pool. The system's robustness depends on feature flags and rollback mechanisms.
